summary: Implemented the two-pass design as a single-file CLI. A registration pass streams all ten tables, normalizes tenant-local person and household IDs, account ledger scopes, order scopes, and device references, and unions alias, merge, and cross-tenant link edges. A compact array-backed disjoint set sits beside an on-disk SQLite key index with a capped page cache. A materialization pass assigns each component a lexical-minimum label and derives a ref_ token; an emission pass re-streams each file, applies every policy transform, and preserves filenames, headers, column order, row order, and row counts. The first subset attempt failed because policy columns hold transform names rather than transform definitions; resolving names through the policy transform table fixed it. The full run processed about 2.08 million rows in about 26 minutes with about 43,500 KB peak RSS, below 64 MB. An independent audit performed about 43 million structural, policy-formula, and cross-file token checks with zero failures and found about 540,000 token classes. Generalized recipe: run the CLI on the full input with a fixed seed, measure peak RSS externally, then independently normalize every policy reference column and assert one token per canonical key plus unchanged structure. Evidence strength is a full-corpus local result; the official verifier was not run and hidden contract semantics remain untested.
next_hint: The full corpus and audit pass. The next question is whether output is deterministic for a fixed seed, whether every seeded transform responds to a seed change, and whether unseeded transforms stay invariant.
